AMENDMENT NO. 1 AUGUST 2003 

TO 

IS 7792 : 1975 CODE OF PRACTICE FOR HANDLING 

PLASTICS CONTAINERS 

( Page 4, clause 3.1.1 ) — Substitute the following for the existing clause: 

3.L1 Small containers (5 litre capacity and below) arc transported in 
polyethylene bags and/or corrugated boxes. However, large containers (above 5 
litre capacity) are transported on light duty one way wooden pallet with shrink 
wrapping or strength wrapping the entire pallet load. 

Note — The use of expendable pallet or paperboard pallet with slip sheet can also be 
considered.'

IS : 7792 - 1975 

Indian Standard 

CODE OF PRACTICE FOR 
HANDLING PLASTICS CONTAINERS 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 26 September 1975, after the draft finalized by the Plastic Containers 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement 
and Packaging Division Council. 

0,2 With the growth of packaging technology the world over, plastics 
containers as available in form of jerrycans, carboys, cannisters, etc, are 
being used more and more for various purposes and are replacing the 
conventional containers of metal, glass, etc. Such plastics containers are 
manufactured indigenously in increasing quantities. Apart from the 
specifications for containers, broad guidelines for proper and safe handling 
of these containers shall assist their increasing use. 

0.3 It is felt that this standard code of practice, which includes the 
guidelines mentioned above, will help the growth of plastics industry on 
sound lines. 



1. SCOPE 

1,1 This standard code of practice covers broadly the safe and proper 
transportation, handling and storage aspects of the plastics containers both 
filled and empty. 

2. STORAGE OF CONTAINERS 
2.1 Storage of Empty Containers 

2.1.1 Containers of less than 5-litre capacity, as far as possible, shall 
not be stacked directly. They should be packed in cardboard cartons 
which can be stacked one above the other. 

2.1.2 Containers over 5-litre capacity may be stacked in a vertical 
position. The only limitation of height of stacking shall be to ensure that 
the bottom piece does not collapse due to the weight of the stack. 

2.1.3 Containers shall not be stored in direct sunlight unless manu- 
factured from the grade incorporating light stabilizer or carbon black well 
dispersed to the extent of minimum of 2*5 percent by weight, 



IS : 7792 . 1975 

2,1 .4 Containers shall be stored away from naked flame. 
2.2 Storage of Filled Containers 

2.2.1 Smaller containers ( 5-litre capacity and below ) shall be packed 
in cardboard boxes for storage. Alternatively, they shall be stored 
individually on shelves and protected from dust by a cover of polyethylene 
film. 

2.2.2 Containers of over 5-litrc capacity shall be stacked vertically one 
over the other up to a height of 5 stacks, depending on the design of the 
container and afler ensuring that the bottom-most container does not 
collapse because of the load. 

Note — The recommended practice for stacking of containers carrying liquid 
chemicals is given below: 

Canity Height of Stacks 
5-litre 5 to 7 high 

10-litre 5 „ 

20-litre 5 „ 

30-Utre 3 to 5 „ 

60-litre and above 2 to 3 ,, 

2.2*3 Containers shall not be stored in the direct sunlight unless manu- 
factured from stabilized grade. Containers containing volatiles should 
not be stored exposed to sunlight or any other source of heat. 

2.2.4 Filled containers shall be stored at a safe distance from flame. 

2.2.5 Filled containers shall be stacked on smooth surface. 

3. TRANSPORT OF CONTAINERS 

3.1 Transport of Empty Containers 

3.1.1 Small containers ( 5-litre capacity and below ) are transported in 
polyethylene liners and/or cardboard boxes and bigger containers ( 10-litre 
capacity and above ) in wooden crates. 

3.1.2 Containers over 5-litre capacity shall be packed in polyethylene 
film bags to protect the containers from dust. 

3.2 Transport of Filled Containers 

3.2.1 Adequate care shall be taken to ensure that there is no leakage of 
contents during storage and transportation. 



IS 1 7792-1975 

3.2.2 The handles may be used for lifting the containers up to a capacity 
of 100 litres. For containers which are to be rolled for handling, rolling 
over any sharp points or edges should be avoided. Adequate care is to be 
taken by providing metal pipes, wooden planks or thick ropes to prevent 
contact against ground. Alternatively, the same may be moved on a 
handcart, platform trolley or by a simpler way by means of hooks suspend- 
ed from a bamboo carried by two people and the containers held by the 
suspended hooks. 

3.2.3 Containers less than 5-litre capacity, when transported in card- 
board boxes, shall be separated by a flat cardboard in between the stacks. 

4. HANDLING OF EMPTY CONTAINERS 

4.1 While loading or unloading, the containers shall not be directly 
' rolled ' on the floor but shall be lifted and carried.
